name: class-person
description: Create a Person class with methods

promptLevels.beginner: make a Person class with name and age
promptLevels.intermediate: create a Person class that stores name, age, and email, and has a method to get person info
promptLevels.advanced: write a class called Person with three properties (name, age, email) and a getInfo method that returns a formatted string with all the person's details
promptLevels.expert: Write a class called `Person` that has three properties: name (string), age (number), and email (string). The constructor should accept these three parameters and assign them to the instance. Add a method called `getInfo()` that returns a formatted string containing all three pieces of information (e.g., "Name: John, Age: 30, Email: john@example.com"). {languageSpecific}

languageInstructions.typescript: Use TypeScript with type annotations for all properties and method return types. Define an interface called `IPerson` that describes the structure of the Person class. The constructor parameters should be typed. Export both the interface and the class.
languageInstructions.javascript: Use ES6 class syntax with a constructor. Export only the class definition. Do not include example usage or console logging.
languageInstructions.javascript-jsdoc: Use JSDoc annotations including @class for the class itself, @typedef or @interface for describing the Person structure, @param for constructor parameters with types, and @returns for the getInfo method. Export only the class.

variants.typescript: Write a TypeScript class called `Person` with properties: name (string), age (number), and email (string). Add a method `getInfo()` that returns a string with the person's details. Include an interface `IPerson` and proper type annotations. Export only the interface and class definitions—do not include example usage, logging, or additional helpers.
variants.javascript: Write a JavaScript class called `Person` with properties: name, age, and email. Add a method `getInfo()` that returns a string with the person's details. Export only the class definition and avoid adding demo code, console logs, or extra exports.
variants.javascript-jsdoc: Write a JavaScript class called `Person` with properties: name, age, and email. Add a method `getInfo()` that returns a string with the person's details. Include JSDoc type annotations with @typedef for a Person type, @class, @param, and @return tags. Output just the class definition—no usage examples or additional modules.

testCases.test: const p = new Person('John', 30, 'john@test.com'); console.assert(p.name === 'John', 'Name should be set');
const p = new Person('John', 30, 'john@test.com'); console.assert(typeof p.getInfo() === 'string', 'getInfo should return string');
const p = new Person('John', 30, 'john@test.com'); console.assert(p.getInfo().includes('John'), 'getInfo should include name');

performanceBenchmarks.name: create-instances
performanceBenchmarks.code: for (let i = 0; i < 100; i++) { new Person('John', 30, 'john@test.com'); }

performanceBenchmarks.name: call-getInfo
performanceBenchmarks.code: const p = new Person('John', 30, 'john@test.com'); for (let i = 0; i < 1000; i++) { p.getInfo(); }
